name: fixed-boundary
title: Rung 1 · Fixed boundary
claim: OBSERVED (partial pass): against an immovable wall mean barrier_velocity = 0 (within ±1e-3) while contact force accumulates. Quantitative match to the Peskin ratchet rate still pending a digitized reference.
decision_figure: tip–wall gap distribution + contact-force accumulation, with Peskin (1993) expected ratchet rate overlaid
expected_pattern: barrier_velocity ≈ 0; contact_force accumulates; tip–wall gap distribution consistent with thermal-fluctuation ratchet
acceptance_threshold: mean barrier_velocity within ±1e-3 AND contact_force > 0 and rising; gap stats within Peskin band
question: Does the composite reproduce the rigid-wall Peskin-1993 regime — Brownian-ratchet kinetics against an immovable boundary — to within numerical tolerance, when barrier_kind is "fixed"?

purpose.question: Does the composite reproduce the rigid-wall Peskin-1993 regime — Brownian-ratchet kinetics against an immovable boundary — to within numerical tolerance, when barrier_kind is "fixed"?
purpose.mechanism: The coupler publishes a fixed wall_z to ReaDDy; actin filaments confined under the wall accumulate contact_force; barrier_velocity stays at zero by construction.
purpose.expected_outcome: contact_force builds up; barrier_velocity ≈ 0; the F-V scatter point sits at velocity≈0, force=mean_contact_force.

variants.name: low-growth
variants.description: Slow polymerization — fewer ratchet events against the fixed wall.

variants.name: high-growth
variants.description: Fast polymerization — higher contact_force buildup at the fixed wall.

tests.name: fv-matches-mogilner-baseline
tests.question: Mean barrier velocity stays at zero (within 1e-3) and mean contact_force is positive across the run, consistent with the rigid-wall ratchet regime.

model_change.notes: Spec §2.2 rung 1. Wall held at fixed z; no membrane process. ReaDDy actin filaments push against the wall via the coupler.

simulation_set.name: rung1-fixed
simulation_set.description: Single closed-loop run with the wall held fixed at z=0. 16 composite steps, interval=0.5.

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Does an immovable barrier produce pure force accumulation with no advance (the classical rigid-wall ratchet limit)?
resolved_uncertainties: Against a fixed wall the barrier velocity holds at ~0 while contact force accumulates (OBSERVED).
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the gap-distribution / ratchet event rate quantitatively match Peskin (1993) — not yet compared to theory.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: The accumulating contact_force is an artefact of wall stiffness (force_constant), not genuine Brownian-ratchet rectification.
evidence_for: contact_force scales with force_constant by construction.
evidence_against: barrier_velocity ~0 and a thermal-fluctuation-shaped gap distribution would argue for true ratcheting.

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: Confirms the rigid-wall baseline: a fixed barrier converts polymerization into accumulated force, not motion.

followup_study_proposals.title: Quantify the tip-wall gap distribution against Peskin theory
followup_study_proposals.expected_information_gain: Turns the OBSERVED velocity~0 into a VALIDATED match (or refutation) of the rigid-wall ratchet rate.
